g1.label: 1. work as ___ in the national parks
g1.why: People who work without pay are volunteers.

g2.label: 2. They do not get any ___
g2.why: They are unpaid, so they get no money — only food and a bed.

g3.label: 3. clean the ___ after big storms
g3.why: Storms wash rubbish onto beaches in Alaska.

g4.label: 4. builds new ___ for walkers
g4.why: Walkers in the mountains need paths.

g5.label: 5. learn a lot about ___
g5.why: Plants, animals and the environment together are nature.

g6.label: 6. sit around a ___
g6.why: An outdoor fire at a camp is a campfire.

g7.label: 7. it is hard ___
g7.why: Hard work collocates here; the jobs are physically demanding.

g8.label: 8. never forget the ___
g8.why: Something you live through and remember is an experience.

g1.label: 1. I enjoy ___ in the mountains
g1.why: 'Enjoy' is always followed by the -ing form, never the infinitive.

g5.label: 5. We avoid ___ plastic bottles
g5.why: 'Avoid' is always followed by the -ing form.

g8.label: 8. He gave up ___ television
g8.why: 'Give up' is a phrasal verb, and verbs after it take -ing.

g1.label: 1. She is good at ___ maps
g1.why: After a preposition such as 'at', the verb takes the -ing form.

g2.label: 2. interested in ___ the environment
g2.why: 'In' is a preposition, so the verb becomes protecting.

g3.label: 3. Instead of ___ the bus
g3.why: 'Of' is a preposition and is followed by the -ing form.

g4.label: 4. Thank you for ___ us
g4.why: 'For' is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing.

g5.label: 5. Before ___ home
g5.why: Before and after take the -ing form when the subject stays the same.

g7.label: 7. We look forward to ___
g7.why: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so the -ing form follows.

g8.label: 8. left the camp without ___ goodbye
g8.why: 'Without' is a preposition and takes the -ing form.
